alex: Evening handoff — short summary of current state.
alex: Incident inc-4536: kvcache thrash in eu-west1. Impact: small-gen latency up ~150-250ms for short requests, error spike to ~2.1%.
alex: Mitigations applied: turned on per-tenant ingest rate-limit at the gateway (temp), scaled +2 kvcache workers in eu-west1, enabled short-lived read-through fallback (flag: kvcache.read_fallback=true).
alex: Observed results ~30m after: p50/p95 back toward baseline for 80% of traffic, error rate down to ~0.6%. Still seeing occasional bursts tied to tenant-19 ingestion.
alex: Immediate next steps: 1) Keep autoscaler at 6m cooldown while we watch (helps absorb spikes). 2) Infra to monitor node disk_io and network queue on nodes 10-14. 3) If recurrence, revert experimental hot-shards change in canary (PR #3419). 4) Maria to watch overnight and run periodic diagnostics.
oncall-bot: Alert summary: 3 alerts closed, 1 active — kvcache-error-rate-eu-west1. Severity: P2. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvcache-thrashing
maria: Ack, I'm on it. I'll run the kv-fast-scan diag every 30m and post results here. Executed runbook step 4 (cleared per-tenant backlog for tenant-19) at +00:12.
maria: Quick question — can infra shorten the autoscaler cooldown to 6m now? Current cooldown is 12m and it's smoothing too slowly.
chris: I applied the 6m cooldown on eu-west1 (infra-oncall). Watching the autoscaler events — will revert if it thrashes. Logs uploaded: https://logs.redwood/ingest/2719876543/summary.log
chris: Quick check command if you want to tail misses: `kubectl -n inference exec -it kvcache-ctrl -- bash -c "curl localhost:9100/metrics | grep kv_cache_miss"`
sam: I can take the 06:00-14:00 shift if anything escalates. FYI PR 3423 (kvcache metrics tags) is awaiting review — it's blocking the dedicated deploy that would give better sharding visibility.
chris: Noted; I'll try to review 3423 in the next hour.
alex: No active customer-facing degradation beyond what's listed. SLA pages unchanged. If error rate > 1.5% or latency p95 > 700ms for >5m, follow emergency rollback (see runbook section 2.1).
alex: Thanks all — leaving handoff to @maria. Ping me if you need context. :thumbsup:
